name: qfd_c_ring516

pin_regs.reason: every data input pin i lands directly in the 4 bank slot registers (enable = registered one-hot), every output pin o is the reader's output register, rsi_w / rsi_r land in the halves' kept reset copies (qfd_c_land_w1k / r1k): flop-first / flop-last, no combinational in->out path

reset_landing.reason: rsi_w / rsi_r are the region-calendar ring resets; each half re-registers them (rq + one kept copy per 30-bit super-group, 1 + NGS = 19 loads) on its own clock -- the parent delivers them from each region's own equal-depth reset tree

structural_change: QW-CB16REG 10-20 main line (a): the CB16 parent's region crossings are hardened as ONE tile per crossing (writer ring qfd_c_land_w1k on the source region clock ck_w + reader qfd_c_land_r1k on the destination region clock ck_r, W=516, D 4, K 2; 69 instances in the parent, 2 masters).  Why: fulln/fullnb/fullm (flat soft rings) gave each region root 6.7k-20.9k ring flops over 1-2 mm -> within-region TT spread 410-813 ps, WNS -1.4..-1.7 ns at the readers after 10-16 h.  Here each tile clock has its own short tree, the bank -> reader path never leaves the tile, and the parent region clock sees one clock pin per ring.  Same function / epochs / latency as the soft pair (0 added cycles).
